item.title: Colombia: el Fondo Milagro y la reconstrucción del terremoto ponen presión a De la Espriella
item.description: La gestión de los recursos para la reconstrucción tras el terremoto enfrenta nuevas críticas. Este viernes renunció el gerente del Fondo Milagro, entidad creada para administrar los recursos destinados a la emergencia, en medio de cuestionamientos por su gestión. La polémica se intensificó tras conocerse los altos salarios de algunos funcionarios y las denuncias sobre el lento avance de las obras. Legisladores señalaron que, más de tres meses después de la catástrofe, el fondo solo había firmado unos pocos contratos para demolición, mientras miles de afectados siguen esperando soluciones. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Gaza enfrenta el invierno entre enfermedades, inundaciones y escasez de ayuda humanitaria
item.description: El frío, las inundaciones y el hacinamiento en los campamentos marcan la cotidianidad de cientos de miles de palestinos en Gaza, en medio de las restricciones israelíes a la entrada de ayuda humanitaria. Estas condiciones favorecen la propagación de enfermedades, especialmente entre niños y adultos mayores.La llegada del invierno también aumenta el riesgo de derrumbes, ahogamientos e hipotermia. Ante esta situación, la ONU reclama el ingreso urgente de ayuda humanitaria al enclave palestino. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.description: The End of Everything is a novel for our age of permacrisis. Genre boundaries belong to the past “Science fiction will never be Literature with a capital ‘L,’” began a New York Times review of Margaret Atwood’s novel Oryx and Crake back in 2003. Now, the seemingly impossible has happened – M John Harrison’s The End of Everything is the first science fiction novel to win the Booker prize. Fans have hailed this as a victory for a long-marginalised genre. item.description: The environmental and economic dilemmas he faces are formidable but, with a bold plan, he could set an example for leaders around the world For politicians of the centre-left especially, it’s the great dilemma of the age. item.title: Cryosphere decline beyond safe planetary limits, putting conditions for human society at risk
item.description: New research published at COP31 issues a stark warning about the health of the frozen parts of the planet—ice sheets, mountain glaciers, sea ice, permafrost and snow cover—known as the cryosphere. The study, published in Science, finds that human-driven climate change is degrading these landscapes beyond safe environmental limits, systematically threatening the Earth system conditions on which humanity fundamentally depends. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: While young people are constantly exposed to news about climate change, their resulting anxiety does not always translate into environmental action. item.title: ‘Incredibly unusual’ bird migrating from Siberia found in Cumbria – killed by cat
item.description: Siberian rubythroat was thousands of miles off course from its route to winter in south or south-east Asia A bird that flies south from its breeding grounds in Siberia to winter in south and south-east Asia has been found thousands of miles off course in Cumbria. Regrettably, it was found by a cat. Chris Hind, Cumbria’s county recorder for birds, said it was “extraordinary” that a Siberian rubythroat was found on his patch, albeit dead. There have been only 17 recorded instances of the bird in the UK, 15 of those in the northern Scottish isles. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: Concrete and steel—or mangroves and forests? When it comes to climate adaptation, nature is much cheaper
item.description: What's the best way to protect ourselves against climate change? The default is to reach for concrete and steel to build seawalls, dikes, dams and drainage systems. These can work. But they are expensive and inflexible. There's another, much cheaper option which gets vastly less attention. Mangroves, forests and urban trees can help protect humans and their homes, farms and cities from floods, droughts, rising seas and heat. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ancient climate records reveal how East Asian monsoon shifted abruptly into cold and drought
item.description: How does climate change affect the East Asian monsoon? Researchers from Utrecht University's Faculty of Geosciences, together with colleagues at research institutes in China and Belgium, are investigating this question by looking back 250,000 years. They found that, over long timescales, the monsoon system tracks changes in incoming solar radiation caused by variations in Earth's orbit and tilt. But when radiation falls below a certain threshold, abrupt periods of extreme cold and drought occur, particularly when atmospheric CO₂ concentrations are low. The study was published in… Fuente: Phys.org.
